newsitem.title: USA: White House Stiglitz says inflation appears stable.
newsitem.headline: White House Stiglitz says inflation appears stable.

text.p: A top White House economic adviser said on Wednesday that there was no evidence of increasing inflationary pressure in the U.S.

"At the present time, there certainly is no evidence of increasing inflationary pressures," Joseph Stiglitz, chairman of the White House Council of Economic Advisers, told Reuters. "Overall, inflation appears to be stable."
Stiglitz made his comments late on Wednesday after he addressed the World Affairs Council in San Francisco.
Stiglitz said the latest U.S. trade deficit figures were not cause for concern.

"You can't put much emphasis on month-to-month numbers," he said. "The fundamentals are what you want to look at. The trade deficit as a percentage of GDP is considerably lower now than it was in the worst years of the 80s."
"If we continue with our strategy of deficit reduction, one of the benefits ... is that it is likely to be associated with a reduction over the long run in the trade deficit," he said.

The Commerce Department said earlier on Wednesday that the U.S. trade deficit soared in July to its highest level in more than eight years as imports surged and foreign sales shrank for a second straight month.

The steep 42.6 percent jump in the July deficit to $11.68 billion from $8.19 billion in June was caused partly by weaker sales of U.S.-made commercial aircraft, as well as brisk demand for Japanese cars and costlier oil.
"Next month could be one way or another," Stiglitz said. "You just don't put a lot of emphasis on any one month's data."
In his address to the World Affairs Council, Stiglitz said the U.S. must continue to work to eliminate the remaining tariff barriers.

"We must continue in our efforts to open international markets to U.S. products and services," he told the group. "It is vital that we continue to move forward, in order to preserve the considerable advances we have already made."
